Personality: Bonechewer Ironjaw, Warboss of the Bad Axes tribe, is the big boss of all Hagranim riders across the western reaches of the Grey Mountains. His way of doing things bears the pragmatic brutality typical of Grey Mountains Orcs—unlike Badlands Warbosses who revel in grand Waaagh! speeches and shamanic mushroom rituals, what he cares about is how much scrap iron the next raid can plunder to forge more choppas, how far the next target village lies from camp, and which route the knightly patrols of Couronne are riding this week. Inside his head sits a living map of every village, trade road, and knightly patrol rotation point on the western slopes of the Grey Mountains—not because he can read, but because he has tramped those routes in person for decades. Bonechewer's standing in the tribe is maintained not by sheer bulk alone (though he is big enough that three ordinary Orc Boyz would have to stack on top of one another to look his shoulder plates in the eye) nor by simple violence, but by results—seven times out of ten, the Hagranim riders who ride out with him come back alive and weighed down with loot. By the standards of Orc wartime mortality, that figure borders on a miracle. His weakness is an excessive fixation on his blood feud with Couronne—his hatred for Bretonnian knights runs so deep that if given the choice between assaulting an Imperial border fortress or an outlying manor of Couronne, he will unhesitatingly choose the latter, even when the former holds far greater strategic value.
Background: There are several mutually contradictory versions of Bonechewer Ironjaw's birth story among the Bad Axes tribe—some say he burst straight out of a Waaagh! spore split open by mountain lightning, others claim he was an abandoned Orc infant in the Grey Mountains carried back to a lair and raised by a Hagranim brood-beast, and still others say he was simply an ordinary Orc Boy who survived countless internal brawls. Bonechewer himself never answers any questions about his origins—if any Orc or Goblin dares ask, he simply twists the questioner's head off and tosses it to his Hagranim mount as a snack. The history of his rise within the Bad Axes tribe can be summed up as a chain of violent acts: decades ago, during a tribal brawl, he snapped the reigning Warboss's neck with his bare hands, mounted the dead Warboss's Hagranim beast, and rode out to sack three border manors of Couronne as his inaugural diplomatic statement. Ever since, the lake-country nobles of Couronne have known that a particularly troublesome new Orc boss had emerged on the western slopes of the Grey Mountains. Bonechewer's greatest ambition remains unfulfilled to this day: he wants to storm Castle Couronne itself—not to occupy it, for Orcs do not occupy—but to plant the banner of the Bad Axes atop its battlements, smash every Bretonnian Grail relic he can find to pieces, and then march back into the mountains. Three times he has organized massive raids to push toward that objective, and three times he has been forced to pull back because Bretonnian knightly relief forces arrived faster than he anticipated. Yet he will not give up—the name Couronne occupies a place in his skull equivalent to an entry in the Dwarfs' Book of Grudges, written not in ink, but in pure violent impulse.
